MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.work: ARMOR: High-Performance Semi-Structured Pruning via Adaptive Matrix Factorization
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.venue: ICLR 2026 Poster -- OpenReview venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, forum 8NE554wv0m. CONFIRMED via the OR-family authority.
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.why_it_matters: THE MOST IMPORTANT OMISSION. ARMOR factorizes each weight matrix into a 2:4 sparse core wrapped by two BLOCK-DIAGONAL matrices, chosen POST-TRAINING by block coordinate descent on a layer-wise proxy loss. That is 2:4-sparse-base + a BLOCK-STRUCTURED (not SVD) low-overhead correction, decided post-training. It is by far the nearest neighbour to B12's operator on surfaces (c)+(d) jointly and it was absent from the file.
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.does_it_preempt: NO, but it narrows the delta and MUST be cited. Three decisive differences: (i) ARMOR's wrappers are CONSTRUCTED one-shot by its own optimisation -- there is no trained branch, so it cannot ask B12's question, which is how much of an ALREADY-TRAINED branch is removable; (ii) ARMOR's wrappers are multiplicative pre/post transformations of the sparse core, a different algebraic form from SLoRB's ADDITIVE branch W*mask + S@B; (iii) ARMOR ADDS capacity to beat 2:4 baselines, B12 REMOVES capacity to titrate a density-quality curve. Opposite direction, same neighbourhood.
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.how_found: abs:'block diagonal' AND abs:'2:4' -> total 2, and abs:'block-diagonal' AND abs:'sparse' AND abs:'pruning' AND abs:'LLM' -> total 1. Both name only ARMOR.

MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.work: LoSA: Dynamic Low-Rank Sparse Adaptation for Large Language Models
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.venue: ICLR 2025 Poster -- OpenReview venueid=ICLR.cc/2025/Conference, forum oXh0939Zzq. CONFIRMED.
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.why_it_matters: Adapters on a SPARSE base with PER-LAYER RANK allocated from layer-wise reconstruction error, and it explicitly solves the merge-back problem (LoRA integrated into the sparse LLM post-training with no added inference latency). That is simultaneously surface (b) non-uniform rank AND surface (d) low-rank on a sparse base. Absent from the file.
MATERIAL_GAPS_FOUND.does_it_preempt: NO. Its rank allocation happens DURING fine-tuning, so its smaller-rank layers are TRAINED at that rank -- the very comparison must_not_claim[0] bars B12 from making. Its sparsity is layer-wise-ratio unstructured, not exact 2:4. But it is the closest prior art for 'non-uniform per-layer adapter rank on a sparse LLM', so B12's asymmetry claim must be stated against it, not only against OWL and PARA.

load_bearing_question.question_verbatim_from_next_gate: whether 'block-basis coarsening of a low-rank branch bolted onto 2:4-sparse weights' is distinct from generic post-hoc adapter-rank reduction
load_bearing_question.answer: DISTINCT, but the distinction is NARROWER than the pre-existing file claimed, and one of its five conjuncts must be downgraded.
reasoning_for_distinct: 1. OPERATOR CLASS. Generic post-hoc adapter-rank reduction is SVD/spectral: keep the top-t singular triplets, store BOTH factors. Every surface-(a) work found (PARA, LoRA-Squeeze, Spectral Surgery, PHLoRA, SpectralLoRA, LoRA-drop, CtM, D-Rank) is in that class. B12's operator replaces the BASIS with a coarser block indicator and refits by least squares; because the coarse basis columns are disjoint and constant-1, the LS solution is closed-form (a block mean) and the basis costs ZERO stored parameters. Verified at source: sparse_modeling.py:886 sets x_proj entries to exactly 1 on-block, and the leg-2 selfcheck measured x_proj on-block min == max == 1.0. Different operator, different cost structure -- not a reparameterisation of SVD.

2. THE OBJECTIVE DIFFERS IN KIND. Generic rank reduction minimises adapter STORAGE at fixed quality. B12's axis is DEPLOYMENT DENSITY in the two-matmul form, bounded below by a hard floor of 50.0% (pure 2:4, zero branch) and above by 63.1011%. That axis only exists because the base is N:M: on a dense base, shrinking an adapter moves storage but not the base's arithmetic density, so the quantity B12 titrates is undefined there. This is the strongest single reason the answer is DISTINCT, and it is measured rather than asserted -- rung A gives back 6.85 density points (63.1011 -> 56.2500) at live_branch_params exactly 404,750,336 (leg-2 selfcheck, int-exact).

3. NOBODY HAS DONE IT TO A TRAINED BRANCH ON AN N:M BASE. The closest works each fail a different necessary condition. SLoPe (ICLR 2025) ADDS an adapter lazily, never removes it. SLiM (ICML 2025) CONSTRUCTS a corrector one-shot, never asks if it is over-provisioned. ARMOR (ICLR 2026) is post-training and block-structured on a 2:4 core, but its wrappers are constructed by its own optimisation -- no trained branch to reduce -- and its form is multiplicative rather than additive. HASSLE-free decomposes a DENSE matrix into 2:4-plus-low-rank. Shears (NAACL 2024 Industry) and LoSA (ICLR 2025) allocate adapter rank DURING training, so their small ranks are trained, not reduced. 37 independent queries aimed at the conjunction returned zero occupants.

4. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS SOUND FOR THE RIGHT REASON. Because the literature's post-hoc adapter operator is uniformly SVD, the density-matched SVD control Dctl carries the PRIOR and coarsening is the challenger. The file gets this right and pre-registers clause_5 accordingly ('If Dctl >= rung P, the verdict is basis coarsening is the wrong operator'). A direction whose own control has the literature's backing is testable rather than rhetorical.
reasoning_against_over_claiming: A. THE ALGEBRAIC FORM IS NOT NOVEL. HASSLE-free's headline config is verbatim a 2:4 sparsity component plus a 64-rank component on Llama3-8B; ARMOR pairs a 2:4 core with block-structured correctors. So 'exactly-2:4 base + additive low-rank term, deployed' is established prior art. Only the POST-HOC REDUCTION OF A TRAINED instance of that form is open.

B. BLOCK STRUCTURE PER SE IS NOT NOVEL. ARMOR's block-diagonal wrappers and 2510.23346's block-diagonal LoRA factors both predate B12. The file's conjunct 3 as written ('the operator is block-basis coarsening, not SVD ... the literature's post-hoc adapter operator is uniformly SVD/spectral') is TRUE only if restricted to operators applied TO A TRAINED ADAPTER. Restricted that way it survives; stated generally it is now false. This conjunct MUST be narrowed.

C. THE SHARED PREMISE IS EXPLICITLY PUBLISHED. LoRA-Squeeze and PrunedLoRA both argue 'learn an expressive higher-rank solution then compress it'. B12's premise is not new; its SETTING and its MEASURED AXIS are.

D. THE ASYMMETRY CLAIM NOW HAS ONE MORE COMPETITOR. The file compares its pre-registered per-family map only to PARA (emergent from a global threshold) and OWL (sparsity axis). LoSA also does non-uniform per-layer adapter rank from measured reconstruction error, on a sparse base. B12's asymmetry is still distinguishable (pre-registered from an exhaustive 5^7 frontier scan, on the basis-WIDTH axis, applied post hoc) but must now be stated against LoSA too.
